thread:
maria: Heads up — p99 token latency on the Token SLI dashboard started spiking in apac-east around 09:10 UTC. Grafana link: https://grafana.internal/d/token-sli/token-sli-overview. Looks correlated with a surge of small-chat workloads (high tokens/sec).

ajay: saw the same. p95 also moved up but p99 has the weird stair-step. Could be shard hot-spotting or vGPU mix (some nodes are running v4 + v100).

chris: ops-bot just fired alert: `TOKEN_P99_REGION_HIGH` at 09:12. payload says region=apac-east, p99=1.2s, tokens_sec spike ~3.6x baseline.

ops-bot: Alert `TOKEN_P99_REGION_HIGH` triggered (severity=warning). Runbook: check shard heatmap, cpu steal, and network egress errors.

luis: quick checks: no recent deploys in apac, busy burst window from customer X test traffic (replayer). I see elevated `kv_cache_miss_rate` on a handful of nodes.

maria: can someone paste the prom query you're using for token p99? mine's:
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, region, instance))
```
but that flattens out per-instance spikes. We should aggregate by shard id not instance.

ajay: try grouping by `shard` label instead:
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, region, shard))
```
then `topk(10, ...)` to surface hot shards.

chris: ran that, top 3 shards in apac-east show p99 around 1.1–1.4s. Those shards are on a mixed vGPU pool with older drivers. Also saw `nvlink_errors_total` bump on two hosts.

luis: interesting — if nvlink errors correlate, network fabric could be causing KV cache retrieval timeouts, which raises token-level tail. Opening infra ticket.

maria: for short-term mitigation can we fold requests off those shards? Smart routing could avoid shards with high p99 via the routing policy. Ajay, can you flip a soft-fallback to uniform routing for 15m?

ajay: yep. I'll update route policy to prefer fresh-shard=true, fallback to uniform for apac-east for 15m. Pushing change now.

deploy-bot: route-policy change deployed by ajay at 09:25 UTC: `apac-east: prefer=fresh-shard, fallback=uniform, ttl=15m`.

maria: after the routing change p99 dropped to ~680ms in the dashboard within 2 mins. tokens/sec still high but tails reduced. :thumbsup:

chris: we should tune the existing `TOKEN_P99_REGION_HIGH` alert — it's firing too early on transient cache misses. Proposal: require p99 > 1.0s for 3m and tokens/sec > 2x baseline. Also add suppression if `kv_cache_miss_rate` < 0.05 to avoid false positives.

luis: agree. Draft PromQL for composite alert:
```
max_over_time(
  (
    (region:token_p99:rate[1m] > 1.0)
    and (increase(tokens_total[5m]) / avg_over_time(tokens_total[30m]) > 2)
    and (avg_over_time(kv_cache_miss_rate[5m]) > 0.05)
  )[3m:1m]
) > 0
```
Not production-ready but captures the intent.

ajay: we'll need to map `region:token_p99:rate` to the histogram_quantile output (we have a recording rule). I'll pair with SLO folks to ensure alert maps to real SLI.

maria: action items: 1) luis open infra ticket for nvlink/network fabric on hosts h-apac-12/13. 2) ajay update routing policy + alert rule change PR. 3) chris add a per-shard heatmap panel to token-sli dashboard showing p50/p95/p99 and kv_cache_miss_rate.

luis: infra ticket here: INFRA-7391 — nvlink errors + host logs attached.

chris: filing the dashboard PR, will include a `heatmap` panel with PromQL:
```
heatmap(
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, shard)),
  by (shard)
)
```
and a companion `kv_cache_miss_rate` overlay.

ajay: i'll open alert PR after pairing with SLO folks. Also re-evaluating threshold by region since apac baseline is 10–20% higher latency due to network geometry.

maria: thanks all. We'll monitor for the next 2 hours. If p99 creeps back above 900ms even after routing, escalate to emergency capacity (spin burst GPUs) and enable permanent shard evacuation for affected hosts.

ops-bot: Monitoring note added to incident timeline. Next check at 09:50 UTC.

maria: final note — let's capture a short postmortem if infra ticket confirms nvlink hardware issue. Otherwise, we need to add automated detection for vGPU driver regressions that cause tail latency.

chris: agreed. I'll start a short doc draft in #postmortems and link here.

luis: ping me if you need logs from h-apac-12/13, I've already started a saved query for `dmesg | grep -i nvidia` and kernel timestamps.

maria: closing thread for now, will re-open if anything regresses. Thanks!
